title: María Pía Santibáñez
text:
I am a fourth-year PhD student in Economics at the University of Chile. Before my PhD, I received an M.A. in Economic Policy from Boston University and a B.A. in Business and Economics from Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María.
My research interests are in applied microeconomics, labor economics, development economics, and economic history.
My current research examines the relationship between parental contact with the justice system and adolescent offending in Chile, as part of a broader agenda on children’s life trajectories and intergenerational disadvantage.
Feel free to reach out at marsantiba@fen.uchile.cl.

title: Research
text:
Status: PhD thesis chapter / Working paper
This study examines intergenerational associations in reported offending in Chile, linking administrative records for the 2010 birth cohort to parental justice-system and school records. The sample comprises adolescents with exactly one registered mother and one registered father; the outcome equals one if the adolescent is named as an alleged offender between January 2024 and March 2025, after reaching the minimum age of criminal responsibility. Parental histories are measured through the day before the child’s 14th birthday.
Any parental reported-offense history is positively associated with adolescent justice-system contact. The association rises sharply with the number and legal severity of parental offenses and is larger for boys, histories involving both registered parents, and offenses associated with a recorded custodial sentence. Multiple-type histories produce the largest typology estimate; neither drug-only nor domestic-violence-only (violencia intrafamiliar, VIF) histories account for the largest associations. The results show that early adolescent justice-system contact is concentrated among families with broader, more persistent, and more serious parental records.
